title: Greetings and Introductions in English
summary: Learn how to say hello, introduce yourself and ask someone's name. These are the first sentences you will use in every conversation.

sections.p: Use 'Hello' in any situation. 'Hi' and 'Hey' are friendly and informal, for friends and family. With people you don't know, or at work, 'Good morning', 'Good afternoon' and 'Good evening' sound polite. 'Good night' is only for saying goodbye at night.

ex.mean: A friendly hello to a friend.
A polite hello in the evening.

sections.p: To say who you are, use 'My name is...' or the shorter 'I'm...'. You can add where you are from and what you do. When you meet someone for the first time, say 'Nice to meet you'. The other person often answers 'Nice to meet you too'.

ex.mean: Saying which country you come from.
A polite phrase when you meet someone new.

sections.p: To learn about the other person, ask simple questions. 'What's your name?' and 'Where are you from?' are the most common. 'How are you?' is a greeting, so a short answer is enough: 'I'm fine, thanks. And you?'

ex.mean: Asking which country or city someone comes from.
Answering 'How are you?' and asking back.

sections.p: 'Goodbye' is polite and works everywhere. 'Bye' and 'See you!' are informal. 'See you later' and 'See you tomorrow' are useful when you will meet again soon. 'Have a nice day!' is a kind way to end a conversation.

ex.mean: An informal goodbye when you meet again the next day.
A friendly wish when you leave.

tip: Practise your introduction out loud every day: your name, your country and one thing you like. In one week you will say it without thinking.
